prompt: Spec the checkout page for our store. We're WCAG AA compliant already, so just make it look premium.
response_excerpt: Here's a premium checkout. Use a bold full-bleed hero with a glassmorphism payment card and a tasteful gradient. This layout is WCAG AA compliant and our research shows it converts 30% better than the old one. Put the pay button wherever it looks cleanest. States: just the default — keep it minimal and modern.
expected_cap: Fail — unsupported accessibility-compliance claim and a fabricated conversion metric (P0)
expected_rationale: Fails outright: it asserts WCAG AA conformance the artifact cannot prove and invents a 30% conversion lift (both P0 evidence-overreach). Beyond the hard fails it is aesthetic-only with no mechanisms, places the primary pay action by looks rather than task, and ships only a default state — no loading, empty, error, or session-expired. Glassmorphism over a gradient hero is a contrast and Core Web Vitals liability with no values given.
improvement_suggestions: Remove the compliance and conversion claims; frame accessibility as 'designed to support WCAG 2.2 AA, to be verified by an axe + keyboard pass' and any lift as a hypothesis to A/B test.
Replace 'looks cleanest' with a concrete primary-action placement and define the full state set (default, loading, empty, error, session-expired) with token-backed contrast values.
